Caption: Study design: questions, monitors, data and status of the analyses.
Table note: Note. Run counts apply to each record; both records of a run come from the same trajectory. Status as in Supplementary Table S1: prespecified, protocol fixed before the runs were generated; follow-up, specified after the recording effect was found and before the monitors were fitted; post hoc, specified after earlier results were known, with evaluation panels reused. Independent streams: one keyed random-number stream per run. The fixed template of family B was chosen after its controller-input Fault 9 results were known. CI, controller-input; PU, post-update; CVA, canonical variate analysis; PCA, principal component analysis; SFA, slow feature analysis.

Caption: Fault 9 under controller-input (CI) and post-update (PU) recording: clean detection within 40 h and 8 h and normal runs with any alarm in 48 h (%).
Table note: Note. In the main analyses, the monitors were trained and calibrated separately for each recording; the fixed public-data monitor (confirmation panel and TEP-Rust) was only recalibrated for each recording, and the matched-FAR rows set limits post hoc on the normal evaluation runs and are descriptive. Normal runs: 400 (five-fit rows and confirmation panel), 120 (recording panel 2) and 60 (TEP-Rust); five-fit rows, means over fits. The all-variable rows and CVA are post hoc. Confirmation panel, prespecified primary endpoint: difference in mean penalized loss (controller-input minus post-update), −1,149.6 min (Bonferroni-adjusted 98.33% interval −1,277.7 to −1,016.4). Multivariate EWMA chart: variant selected among 22 multivariate charts on the labelled selection runs of each recording (post hoc; Supplementary Section S5.2). CVA: lags and state order fixed before fitting; refitted on 78 normal runs with independent streams, it detected 9.5% and 8.0% of the runs within 40 h at FARs of 8.75% and 6.75% (Supplementary Section S5.5). Other monitors, counts and intervals: Supplementary Sections S5 and S10.

Caption: Faults 3 and 15 on the independent-stream confirmation panel: clean detection within 40 h and 8 h and normal runs with any alarm in 48 h (%).
Table note: Note. Confirmation panel: 200 runs per fault and 400 normal runs with independent streams. Family A and the classifier were fitted once per record on the Fault 3 or Fault 15 development runs (Section 3.1) and only recalibrated on the 199 normal calibration runs of the panel; SFA, means over five fits on normal runs. Family A starts monitoring at the first record, SFA and the classifier at the 40th. Post hoc; the classifier results depend on its CUSUM reference value k. Identity-metric variants, other settings and intervals: Supplementary Section S10.

Caption: Normal data under the unchanged public-data Fault 9 score map.
Table note: Note. Samples 161–960 of each normal run. Score variance is βᵀCβ for fixed coefficients β and covariance C; the increase of 2.3712 splits into +0.2802 from diagonal and +2.0910 from cross-covariance terms. The two panels are not paired.

Recording panel 2, separate chart comparison on the fixed public-data score: Fault 9 results.

Caption: Standard monitors retrained and calibrated on each recording (all 52 variables): Fault 9 results.
Table note: Note. Limits: 57th of 59 normal calibration run maxima (panel 1) and 190th of 199 (panel 2), for each recording and monitor. Pre-fault alarms and misses count as 2,400 min and remain in all denominators.

Caption: Supervised monitors relearned on each recording: Fault 9 results of the relearning experiment.
Table note: Note. All four monitors use the signed score and were learned once on the same 306 development runs, after the amendment described in the text (16 retained residual dimensions under post-update and 15 of 17 under controller-input recording). Limits are the 190th of 199 (panel 2) and the 57th of 59 (panel 1) normal calibration run maxima for each monitor, frozen before the evaluation runs were scored. Caption: Independent relearning on new runs: operating points of the four monitors of each fit (counts of runs).
Table note: Note. 200 Fault 9 and 400 normal evaluation runs, shared by all fits and monitors; each run was recorded both ways. In every fit, PCA retained 35 components under controller-input and 36 under post-update recording, and 15 and 16 residual dimensions remained after the normal-support restriction. All monitors use the signed score and the original estimate of B. Each limit h is the 190th of the 199 normal calibration-run maxima of its monitor. Clean detections require no alarm in records 1–160; pre-fault alarms and misses count as 2,400 min in the mean loss.

Caption: Independent relearning on new runs: controller-input minus post-update contrasts, averaged over the five fits.
Table note: Note. Rates and losses averaged over the five fits; differences in percentage points (minutes for the loss). Intervals: percentile intervals from 20,000 paired bootstrap draws of whole runs (200 Fault 9 runs; 400 normal runs for the last two rows of each pool), with the same draws for all monitors and fits, conditional on the five fits and the common calibration runs. The second-moment rows for detection within 40 h and for normal runs with any alarm are the prespecified primary and risk contrasts; the other rows are supportive and unadjusted. Fits +/0/−: number of fits with a positive, zero or negative difference. The detection floor is the fraction of normal runs with no alarm in records 1–160 and at least one afterwards.

Caption: Faults 3 and 15 under both recordings: frozen monitors on the 120 new fault and 120 reused normal evaluation runs.
Table note: Note. Counts of fault runs with a clean detection within 40 h, 8 h and 2 h, and of normal runs with any alarm in 48 h; mean loss over the 120 fault runs. Each fault and recording has its own learned monitors and limits (190th of 199 normal calibration-run maxima). The C1 comparator applies the squared score to the direction selected for the signed score in the mean-shift pool; the C3 comparator is the mean-shift pool with the squared score.

Caption: Faults 3 and 15 under both recordings: paired contrasts on the evaluation runs.
Table note: Note. Paired 95% percentile intervals from 20,000 bootstrap draws of the 120 fault and 120 normal evaluation runs, pointwise and conditional on one learned pipeline per fault and recording; they are not the Bonferroni-adjusted intervals of the original validations. Rows between recordings compare separately learned pipelines on the same physical runs and are descriptive. pp, percentage points.

Caption: Multivariate charts without learned directions under both recordings: counts on the evaluation runs.
Table note: Note. One learned replicate per recording; 120 fault and 120 reused normal evaluation runs (follow-up for Faults 3 and 15, recording panel 2 for Fault 9). Counts of fault runs with a clean detection within 40 h and 8 h and of normal runs with any alarm. The multivariate charts have limits at the 190th of the 199 panel-2 calibration run maxima, and the selected variant may differ between recordings. The other monitors keep their archived results (Faults 3 and 15: Section S5.2; Fault 9: Section S5.1). Last column: learned-direction monitor minus U* in mean loss with paired 95% percentile intervals from 20,000 bootstrap draws of the physical runs (fault and normal runs resampled separately), pointwise and unadjusted.

Caption: Independent-stream confirmation panel: the three primary contrasts of mean penalized loss over 40 h.
Table note: Note. Paired percentile intervals from 20,000 bootstrap draws of whole runs; for C1 and C3, each run’s difference was averaged over the five replicates before resampling. A contrast is supported when its adjusted interval lies entirely on the predicted side of zero. Intervals are conditional on the frozen monitors and the fixed limits.

Caption: Partial sharing of measurement noise: the fixed public-data Fault 9 monitor on the independent-stream panel (counts of runs).
Table note: Note. 199 normal calibration, 400 normal and 200 Fault 9 evaluation runs. Shared components: original noise uniforms kept in each recorded measurement-noise value (ρ = shared/12). The five shared-noise settings use the controller-input measurement times and the original process trajectories and valve outputs; the ρ = 1 and actual post-update rows reproduce the fixed public-data monitor results of Table S15. Each limit h is the 190th of the 199 normal calibration-run maxima of its setting. Normal score variance: pooled sample variance of the fixed score over all 960 records of the 400 normal evaluation runs. Clean detections require no alarm in records 1–160; pre-fault alarms and misses count as 2,400 min in the mean loss. Wilson 95% intervals of the rates: Fig. S4.

Caption: TEP-Rust: the fixed public-data Fault 9 monitor under the controller-input and standard records (counts of runs).
Table note: Note. 59 normal calibration, 60 normal and 75 Fault 9 evaluation runs of TEP-Rust, each recorded both ways from the same trajectory. Both records are scored with the fixed public-data Fault 9 monitor; each limit h is the 57th of the 59 calibration-run maxima of its record. Clean detections require no alarm in records 1–160, with delays counted from record 161 (Section S3.2); counted from the activation of the fault, the controller-input record detected 21 instead of 22 runs within 8 h. Normal score variance: pooled over all 960 records of the 60 normal runs. Pre-fault alarms and misses count as 2,400 min in the mean loss.

Caption: Monitors produced when the four workflows were rebuilt from post-update records. Not produced: the frozen rule declined to construct a monitor. For OOF, “default set after joint comparison” means at least four eligible families, a legal default set and no passing challenger; “fallback set” means the legal alternative with the highest ϕ after an illegal default set (Section S4.5); “no legal candidate set” means eligible families but no candidate set that met the eligibility conditions in its joint out-of-fold evaluation. Rank is the dimension of a produced monitor.

Rebuilding from post-update records: endpoints at calibration rank 95. Mean loss and clean detection are means over all 36 replicates, with replicates without a monitor counted as 483 min and no detection, and descriptive two-sided 95% crossed-bootstrap intervals; “available monitors” gives the mean clean detection within 8 h over the monitors produced, with their number. Where any monitor is missing, the normal alarm rate and the detection floor are undefined (NA) for the 36-replicate design; the mean over the monitors produced and their number are given in parentheses, without an interval.

Post-update minus controller-input recording for the same workflow, replicates and physical trajectories at calibration rank 95, with descriptive two-sided 95% crossed-bootstrap intervals; pp, percentage points. Positive loss differences and negative detection differences mean poorer performance with post-update records.
Recording combinations and their source identifiers. A denotes controller-input recording and N denotes post-update recording.

Recording combinations at rank 95. Each cell gives clean detection within 8 h (%), clean detection within 40 h (%) and available reconstructions (of 36), in that order. Detection uses the full denominator of 4,320.
Rank-95 factorial contrasts for clean detection within 8 h (percentage points, descriptive 95% crossed-bootstrap intervals). Positive main effects favour controller-input recording.

FT after deleting XMEAS12, XMEAS15, XMEAS17, XMV7, XMV8 and XMV11, with all remaining variables retained in the stated recording convention. Rates are percentages at rank 95. Replicates without a monitor count as no detection (denominator 36 × 120). Post hoc analyses specified on 28–29 October 2026.

Table note: Note. All 36 replicates produced a monitor for every variant; each chart was calibrated with the run-level rule of main-text Section 3.3. Post hoc analysis.

Clean detection (%) at rank 95 with XMEAS2 exchanged. The normal column gives the normal alarm rate. The last column counts reconstructions with fewer than 108 clean detections among 120 trajectories at 40 h. All 36 reconstructions were available in each row.

Variable participation in the subspaces of the produced monitors: number of monitors, ranks of XMEAS17 and XMV11 among the 52 variables, and the six largest mean normalized participations Pⱼⱼ/r, averaged over the monitors produced.
Post-update minus controller-input records of XMEAS12 and XMEAS15 in the paired normal simulations: the variance of the difference split into measurement noise and process change.
Table note: Note. Variances over all 960 records of the runs in each panel (ddof = 0), in squared measurement units. The three parts add to the variance of the difference; the shares are variance-accounting ratios, not independent causal fractions. The nominal noise standard deviation of both measurements is 1, so two independent draws give a difference variance of 2.

Caption: Measurement–valve correlations in the process-backend check and in archived normal data, median [range] over runs.
Table note: Note. Backend rows: 48-h runs with the same unmodified package driver, Python controllers and passive observer for both backends; under controller-input recording, every run exceeded 0.99999. Archived rows: correlations computed on the saved records without regenerating them; the Reinartz et al. data were generated with a different control structure.

Caption: Post-update minus controller-input differences of the ten flow and two level measurements in the 400 normal evaluation runs of the independent-stream panel, split into measurement noise and process change.
Table note: Note. Variances over all 960 records of the 400 runs (ddof = 0), in units of the nominal noise variance of each measurement. Noise part, variance of the noise difference; process part, variance of the difference of the process values without additive noise. The three parts add to the variance of the difference; the shares are variance-accounting ratios, not causal fractions. The ten other continuously evaluated measurements and the 19 composition measurements, which were identical under the two recordings, are given in the archived data.

Caption: Score variance of the fixed public-data Fault 9 monitor in the 400 normal evaluation runs of the independent-stream panel under measurement substitutions, and decomposition of the difference between post-update and ρ = 0 records.
Table note: Note. Pooled score variances over all 960 records of the 400 runs (ddof = 1; with 384,000 records, ddof = 0 as in Table S32 would multiply every value by 1 − 2.6 × 10⁻⁶), with the affine score map and the valve outputs unchanged. Substitutions replace the named measurements of each post-update record by their controller-input values; bridge records keep the independent noise of the ρ = 0 records and take the named process values from the post-update records. Allocation: 2Cov(s₀, Tⱼ) + Cov(Tⱼ, T), where s₀ is the score of the ρ = 0 record, Tⱼ the score change from replacing the process value of measurement j and T = Σⱼ Tⱼ; the remaining endpoint covariance blocks sum to 0.006. Intervals: percentile intervals from 20,000 paired bootstrap draws of whole runs, descriptive and conditional on the frozen monitor and the noise realization.

Caption: Exchanging XMEAS17 between the recordings: two frozen Fault 15 monitors (counts of runs).
Table note: Note. 120 paired follow-up Fault 15 runs and 120 paired normal evaluation runs of recording panel 2. The base recording determines the other 51 inputs, the transformation and the original limit (190th of 199 normal calibration-run maxima); only XMEAS17 is taken from the stated recording. A clean detection requires no alarm in records 1–160 and a first alarm within the stated time after onset at record 161; normal alarms count runs with any crossing in 48 h. Neither monitor was refitted or recalibrated on the hybrid records.

CI, controller-input; PU, post-update; pp, percentage points.

Caption: Monitors of Faults 3 and 15 transferred unchanged to the confirmation panel and recalibrated there (%).
Table note: Note. 200 runs per fault and 400 normal runs of the confirmation panel; one fit per fault and recording, developed on the runs of Section S5.2; limits, the 190th of the 199 normal calibration-run maxima of the confirmation panel. Table note: Note. Means over 36 replicates on the 120 extended fault runs of each fault and the normal evaluation panel of each stage; limits, the 95th of the 99 normal calibration-run maxima of each replicate; monitoring from record 40. Caption: Clean detection at matched false-alarm rates (%).
Table note: Note. Limits set for each fit on the normal evaluation runs (family A: 400 runs; family B: 120 runs per panel) to give the stated fraction of normal runs with any alarm in 48 h; descriptive. Caption: Precision of the controller-input measurements: the five Fault 9 monitors of family A after rounding or a deadband (%).
Table note: Note. Only the 41 measurements of the controller-input record were compressed; the valve outputs kept their archived precision. Each monitor was recalibrated at each step (190th of the 199 normal calibration-run maxima); means over the five fits on 200 Fault 9 and 400 normal evaluation runs, with the windows of Section S3.2. On the post-update record, the same monitors detected 1.3% and 14.6% of the runs within 8 h and 40 h at a FAR of 6.25%. SD, standard deviation.

Caption: Paired fault displacement and normal variation along fixed directions: controller-input divided by post-update record, first 8 h after onset.
Table note: Note. 12 seed groups with common random numbers (Section S6.6), re-recorded at the 3-s phase of the main experiments; records 160–319. Fixed template: 36 maps per fault and training recording, coordinates in training-normal score SD; family A: the five learned-direction Fault 3 monitors and the fixed public-data Fault 9 monitor of the confirmation panel. Ratios with 95% percentile intervals from 20,000 bootstrap draws of seed groups; the intervals of the RMS ratios lie within 0.9999–1.0002. RMS, root mean square; SD, standard deviation.

Caption: Recomputing XMEAS2 from post-update records: the fixed template of family B, clean detection within 2, 8 and 40 h and FAR (%).
Table note: Note. The fixed template was refitted and recalibrated for each record in 36 replicates; 120 extended runs per fault and the normal evaluation panel of each stage; monitoring from record 40. The post-update record with the stored controller-input XMEAS2 gave the same first alarms as the record with the recomputed XMEAS2. Means over replicates with 95% crossed-bootstrap percentile intervals (20,000 draws).
